flashcard_questions.q: Which weekly wage does Scrooge pay Bob Cratchit?
Which line of Marley’s shows he now regrets neglecting other people?
How long has Jacob Marley been dead when his ghost appears?
What does Marley’s chain of cash-boxes and ledgers symbolise?
flashcard_questions.a: The moral burden built up by a lifetime of greed.

flashcard_questions.q: Which words does Tiny Tim speak that capture his generosity and innocence?
What does Tiny Tim’s ‘withered little hand’ symbolise?
flashcard_questions.a: Premature decay caused by poverty, like a flower denied light.

flashcard_questions.q: Which image does the Ghost of Christmas Present use to warn of Tiny Tim’s death?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘I see a vacant seat … and a crutch without an owner.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which toast does Bob Cratchit make to Scrooge at Christmas dinner?
Why does Belle end her engagement to Scrooge?
flashcard_questions.a: He has let ‘another idol’, ‘a golden one’, displace her — he chose wealth.

flashcard_questions.q: Who is Fred’s mother, the sister Scrooge loved?
What streams from the head of the Ghost of Christmas Past?
flashcard_questions.a: A bright clear jet of light.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the empty scabbard worn by the Ghost of Christmas Present symbolise?
flashcard_questions.a: Christmas as a time of peace.

flashcard_questions.q: Which single gesture does the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come use instead of speech?
What is a foil in a novel?
flashcard_questions.a: A character who contrasts with another, making each one’s qualities more visible.

flashcard_questions.q: Which former employer throws a lavish Christmas party for his workers?

notes: 15 cards: 5 quotation-recall fronts (Marley, Tiny Tim, the vacant seat, Bob’s toast, Belle), 4 symbol-to-meaning (the chain, the withered hand, the scabbard, the pointing finger), 3 character facts (fifteen shillings, seven years, Fezziwig), 1 character relationship (Fan), 1 description card (the jet of light), 1 term-to-definition (foil). ‘Ebenezer Scrooge’, ‘Bob Cratchit’, ‘Tiny Tim’, ‘cornucopia’ and ‘symbol’ dropped as glossary restatements or flavour; the stave-by-stave arc was left out because it can only be answered as an enumeration. All quotations verbatim from the lesson content.
